title: The City's $154 million Coronavirus Relief Fund: who is named
question: Who received the City's share of the 2020 federal Coronavirus Relief Fund, by the City's own final report?
finding: The City received $153.8 million. Its final report gives one line with no recipient named for $116.8 million (76%); the remaining lines name 13 recipients for $37.0 million, including $12.2 million to 4 protective-equipment suppliers that the City ledger shows were paid $35.2 million in fiscal 2020 and 2021. Taken with the $624.8 million recovery grant reported as a single line, $741.7 million of the $778.6 million in the City's two largest pandemic grants (95%) has no named recipient in the federal files. For the recovery grant, 30 of the 39 other large California cities and counties reported 1,417 named subawards to the Treasury by mid-2023; San Francisco reported none.
how: Every row of the federal oversight committee's final Coronavirus Relief Fund data where the City is the prime recipient (31 rows for the period ending 30 September 2021), added up by recipient with the correction rows netted in. City payments are every ledger payment to a vendor of the same name; where the ledger uses a different name for the same recipient, the name counted is shown.
limits: The Treasury let governments report payments to individuals, which can include a government's own public-safety payroll, as one total, and money taken as revenue replacement carries no recipient reporting at all. The single lines are why the federal files cannot show who was finally paid. A supplier paid more by the City than its relief-fund award was simply paid partly from other money. Ledger names are matched by hand and are name matches. The City's own ledger and audits are the place to trace these payments.
